item.title: Evanston: Calgary's Best Family Neighbourhood Guide (2026)
item.description: Explore Evanston, Calgary — top schools, 16+ parks, modern homes from $500K, and easy Stoney Trail access. Your 2026 neighbourhood guide by Raman Basra.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Evanston, Calgary

If you're searching for Evanston Calgary homes, you've landed on one of northwest Calgary's most beloved family communities. Tucked near the city's northern edge, Evanston blends modern suburban living with a genuine neighbourhood feel that keeps residents planting roots for years. Whether you're a young family, a move-up buyer, or an out-of-province newcomer, Evanston delivers newer builds, excellent schools, and green space in abundance — all at prices that still make sense in today's market. As a Calgary real estate professional, Raman Basra has helped countless buyers find their perfect home in Evanston, and this guide covers everything you need to know before making your move.

Location & Getting Around

Evanston sits in the northwest quadrant of Calgary, positioned almost perfectly halfway between downtown Calgary and the city of Airdrie. Stoney Trail (Calgary's ring road) runs along the community's southern border, giving residents fast access to both the rest of the city and Highway 2 north. Commutes to the downtown core typically run 25–35 minutes by car, and the Symons Valley Road corridor connects directly to major employment centres. Calgary Transit serves the area with several routes, and the planned BRT expansion is expected to improve connectivity further in the coming years.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Evanston is a community that takes pride in its people. With a strong contingent of young families and professionals, the neighbourhood buzzes with activity throughout all four Calgary seasons. The Evanston Community Association organizes seasonal events, cleanup days, and neighbourhood gatherings that build genuine connections between residents. Two senior living residences — Evanston Grand Village and Evanston Summit — make the community especially welcoming for multi-generational families who want loved ones nearby. The elevated West Lookout Point at the community's edge offers panoramic views of the northwest, and is a favourite spot for morning walks and evening strolls. Overall, the vibe here is friendly, active, and decidedly family-oriented without feeling too quiet or suburban-sleepy.

Schools & Education

Evanston is exceptionally well-served for education. On the public side, Kenneth D. Taylor School (CBE, K–Grade 4) is located within the community, and the brand-new Evanston Heights School — a CBE middle school serving Grades 4 to 8 — opens in the 2026–2027 school year, a significant win for families who previously had to bus children out of the area. For Catholic families, the Calgary Catholic School District operates Our Lady of Grace School, St. Josephine Bakhita School, St. Thomas Aquinas School (K–9), and St. Luke School (K–6) in and around the community. High school students typically attend W. P. Wagner or St. Francis for Catholic programming.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Evanston punches well above its weight when it comes to green space. The community boasts 16 parks, 7 playgrounds, and over 6.3 kilometres of connected pathways — impressive for a newer neighbourhood. The central Evanston Community Park features a large playground, picnic shelter, basketball court, firepit, and a beloved community garden. The Evanston Pond & Wetland is a scenic stormwater feature ringed by walking paths, benches, and interpretive wildlife signage — a genuine natural amenity in the middle of the suburbs. For those who love a view, the West Lookout Point delivers sweeping panoramas year-round. Nearby, Nose Hill Park — one of Calgary's largest urban parks — is only minutes away for hikers and dog walkers.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Day-to-day errands are a breeze from Evanston, thanks primarily to Creekside Shopping Centre at Stoney Trail and Symons Valley Road NW. The centre anchors a Co-op grocery and Shoppers Drug Mart for everyday needs, alongside dining options including Boston Pizza, Blowers & Grafton (East Coast comfort food), Subway, KFC, and Taco Bell. Health and wellness is covered by Creekside Medical Clinic, Chatters Hair Salon, and Serene Escapes Day Spa. The Evanston Plaza adds further retail variety closer to the community's core. For larger shopping runs, CrossIron Mills and the many big-box retailers along Country Hills Boulevard are just a short drive away.

Real Estate in Evanston

The Evanston Calgary real estate market remains one of the most active in the northwest, and for good reason. The community is dominated by single-detached homes built primarily between 2008 and the present, meaning buyers benefit from modern floor plans, energy-efficient construction, and minimal deferred maintenance compared to older Calgary communities.

Pricing breakdown (mid-2026):

  • Entry-level detached homes (older or smaller builds): $500,000–$599,000
  • Mid-range detached (most active price band): $600,000–$750,000
  • Premium and newer builds: $750,000–$900,000+
  • Townhomes and semi-detached: $400,000–$550,000

The median sold price in April 2026 was approximately $638,000, with average asking prices running around $653,000 as of August 2026. Evanston homes typically trade near or slightly below the Calgary city benchmark, making them attractive value compared to inner-city and established NW communities like Tuscany or Rocky Ridge.

Market conditions in Evanston have stabilized after the sharp appreciation of 2021–2023. Demand remains healthy, driven by Calgary's growing population, strong in-migration from other provinces, and continued affordability relative to Vancouver and Toronto. Homes in good condition and priced correctly are selling within two to four weeks. Inventory has increased modestly in 2026, giving buyers slightly more selection without dramatically softening prices.

For investors, Evanston's family-friendly profile and school catchment quality support solid rental demand, particularly for larger detached homes.

Why Choose Evanston?

  • Newer housing stock — Modern builds mean lower maintenance costs and better energy efficiency compared to older Calgary communities.
  • Outstanding schools — Multiple CBE and CSSD options within the community, plus a brand-new middle school opening in fall 2026.
  • Green space in abundance — 16 parks, 7 playgrounds, 6.3 km of pathways, and proximity to Nose Hill Park.
  • Strong value — Quality homes at prices below comparable communities in west and inner-city Calgary.
  • Excellent connectivity — Direct Stoney Trail access puts the whole city (and Airdrie) within easy reach.
